compiled_state.description:
## Problem

`fixture_selection.select_from_corpus` eagerly compiles full ticket state for EVERY
review-bearing ticket before selection, via `reader(ticket_id, tracker)` (default
`labels._read_ticket_state_via_env_override`, which calls `show_ticket(ticket_id,
include_inbound=True)`). At full corpus scale this is ~6s/ticket x ~1957 unique tickets
≈ **~3 hours of pure CPU** before a single candidate is emitted — and the live admission
runner (`fixture_admission`) pays this same cost upfront on every run.

Measured this session (impl-693 worktree, full committed corpus): a single
`_read_ticket_state_via_env_override` call is ~5–7s; the selection loop compiled state for
1957 unique tickets; a stubbed reader completes the identical candidate selection in ~57s.

## Why it's expensive and why it's avoidable

`ticket_state` is consumed in selection ONLY by `_escaped(review)` →
`labels.escaped_defect(state)`, which needs just two things: `close_class == "plan_defect"`
and any inbound `caused_by` link. The full `show_ticket(include_inbound=True)` reducer is far
more than that. The candidate SET and tier split are provably independent of ticket_state
(tier derives from fire/no_fire signals: reproduction/author_response/margin); `escaped_defect`
only affects the rank tiebreak (2nd sort key in `_candidate_sort_key`).

The corpus event loader (`corpus._load_ticket_events`) does NOT carry STATUS/LINK events, so a
cheap batched `escaped_defect` index cannot be built from it directly — the fix needs either a
batched store read of close_class + caused_by edges, or lazy per-ticket compilation restricted
to only the tickets actually referenced by emitted candidates.

## Approach

Compile `escaped_defect` (or the minimal ticket_state it needs) lazily/batched instead of
eagerly for all review-bearing tickets:
- Option A (lazy): defer state compilation until a review is about to become an emitted
  candidate, so only the small candidate-referenced ticket set pays the cost.
- Option B (batched): one store-wide pass building `{ticket: close_class}` and a reverse
  `caused_by` index, then an O(1) `escaped_defect` lookup per ticket.

Preserve behaviour: candidate set, tiers, ranks (incl. escaped-defect promotion) must be
byte-identical to the current eager path over the same committed history.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `select_from_corpus` over the full committed corpus completes in minutes, not hours,
      with NO per-review-bearing-ticket `show_ticket(include_inbound=True)` fan-out — verified
      by a test asserting the reader/compile is invoked only for candidate-referenced tickets
      (or replaced by a batched index), not for all review-bearing tickets.
- [ ] Emitted manifest rows (candidate set, tier, direction, rank, escaped_defect) are
      byte-identical to the current implementation over a fixed fixture corpus — verified by a
      regression test comparing old vs new output.
- [ ] `escaped_defect` fidelity is preserved: a ticket closed `plan_defect`, and a ticket named
      by an inbound `caused_by`, both still rank-promote — verified by a held-out test.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`
      pass.

## Provenance

Discovered during REB-693 (epic 65dd / spin-cub-usher) ticket 67aa AC10: the live admission
run's selection step took >54 min CPU and was on track for ~3h before the norm-less findings
even reached the solver. The AC10 live run was completed with a stubbed `read_ticket_state`
(escaped_defect=False) as a documented fidelity compromise (candidate set + tiers identical;
rank tiebreak only); this ticket is the real-fidelity + performance fix.

file_impact.reason: replace eager per-ticket state compilation with lazy/batched escaped_defect
provide a batched or cheaper escaped_defect reader path

compiled_state.title: select_from_corpus eagerly compiles ticket state for all review-bearing tickets (~3h at full scale)
